- Modern economics **is** computational: models without closed-form solutions, large datasets, simulations
- One skill, many uses: research, central banks, consulting, data science
- This course: **Julia** — reads like maths, runs like C

## Why Julia?

| | Python | MATLAB | Julia |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speed | slow loops | licensed | fast |
| Syntax | good | maths-like | maths-like |
| Cost | free | ££ | free |
| Used at | everywhere | legacy | central banks, QuantEcon |

## Variables

```{.julia}
gdp = 2.85e12
α = 0.3          # Unicode! type \alpha + TAB
β = 0.96
```

- No type declarations needed — Julia infers them
- Underscores in big numbers: `68_350_000`

## The Solow model in six lines

```{.julia}
function solow_path(; s=0.25, α=0.3, δ=0.05, k0=1.0, T=100)
    k = zeros(T); k[1] = k0
    for t in 1:T-1
        k[t+1] = s*k[t]^α + (1-δ)*k[t]
    end
    return k
end
```

$$k_{t+1} = s\,k_t^{\alpha} + (1-\delta)k_t$$
